title: Do the digits 7, 0 and 5 always make one number?
description: The digits seven, zero and five are read three ways, as hundreds and ones, as tens and tenths, and as units and hundredths. Each reading is written as a number with the place of each digit shown. Keeko's doubt is that all three are the same quantity because the digits match.
teaching_notes: One idea: the decimal point fixes the place of every digit, so the same digits can give very different quantities. Watch for students who think the same digits always mean the same quantity.

source: The digits 7, 0 and 5 can mean 7 hundreds and 5 ones, or 7 tens and 5 tenths, or 7 units and 5 hundredths.
video_script.why: The child knows tenths and hundredths as parts of a unit and now writes them with a decimal point.
video_script.substitution: The decimal point sits after the units place, so each digit's place tells its value.
video_script.anchor: a place value chart with hundreds, tens, units, a point, tenths and hundredths
video_script.wrong_move: reads three numbers with the same digits as one quantity
video_script.payoff_line: The point shows which place each digit holds

final_answer.spoken: seven hundred five, seventy point five and seven point zero five

video_script.fraction_reading: tenths and hundredths are said as words
maths_rules: the point sits after the units place; places to its right are smaller than one
the slip: the same digits in different places give different quantities
video_script.design: The place value chart stays on the stage; the same three digits slide into three different sets of places, and the working band builds each number. Keeko's doubt sets the three side by side.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book, then the digits 7, 0 and 5 with three readings: 7 hundreds and 5 ones, 7 tens and 5 tenths, 7 units and 5 hundredths; a question mark in the anchor band

marks.read: the three readings are written under the digits

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about the digits seven, zero and five.
<bookmark mark='read'/>These digits can mean seven hundreds and five ones. They can also mean seven tens and five tenths, or seven units and five hundredths.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Write each quantity as a number and say where each digit sits.

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board; Keeko sits beside it as the child
narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a place value chart: hundreds, tens, units, then a point, then tenths and hundredths

marks.chart: the chart of places is drawn
marks.point: the point is drawn after the units place

narration: <bookmark mark='chart'/>Here is a place value chart with hundreds, tens, units, tenths and hundredths.
<bookmark mark='point'/>The point sits after the units place, and the places to its right are smaller than one.

beats.on_screen: Given: the digits 7, 0 and 5 read in three ways
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the digits seven, zero and five, read in three different ways.

beats.on_screen: To find: each quantity as a number, with the place of each digit
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to write each quantity as a number and show the place of each digit.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: 7 hundreds, 0 tens, 5 ones: 700 + 0 + 5 = 705; no point is needed

marks.hundreds: 7, 0 and 5 slide into hundreds, tens and ones

narration: <bookmark mark='hundreds'/>Step one, seven hundreds, zero tens and five ones make seven hundred plus zero plus five.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>That is seven hundred five, and no point is needed here.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: 7 tens, 0 units, 5 tenths: 70 + 0 + 5/10 = 70.5; the 7 is tens, the 0 is units, the 5 is tenths

marks.tens: 7, 0 and 5 slide into tens, units and tenths
marks.places: each digit is labelled with its place

narration: <bookmark mark='tens'/>Step two, seven tens, zero units and five tenths make seventy plus zero plus five tenths.
<bookmark mark='write'/>We write it as seventy point five.
<bookmark mark='places'/>The seven is in tens, the zero is in units, and the five is in tenths.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: 7 units, 0 tenths, 5 hundredths: 7 + 0/10 + 5/100 = 7.05; the 7 is units, the 0 is tenths, the 5 is hundredths

marks.units: 7, 0 and 5 slide into units, tenths and hundredths
marks.write: 7.05 is written with the zero in the tenths place

narration: <bookmark mark='units'/>Step three, seven units, zero tenths and five hundredths make seven plus zero plus five hundredths.
<bookmark mark='write'/>We write it as seven point zero five, with the zero holding the empty tenths place.

marks.ans: the three numbers are boxed side by side

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The point shows which place each digit holds.
The quantities are seven hundred five, seventy point five and seven point zero five.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the place value chart
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: 705, 70.5 and 7.05 side by side with an equals sign struck out; each digit shows its own place

marks.doubt: an equals sign appears between the three numbers
marks.fix: the equals sign is struck out and the places are shown

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks all three are the same quantity, because they use the same digits.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But each digit takes its value from its place. The point fixes the places. Three different places make three different quantities.
